To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RNA helicase DHX-15 is required for the activation of the MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways downstream of the adaptor protein MAV-5 and is required for MAVS-mediated apoptosis.
DHX15 is an activator of MAPKs and NF-κBs, and that it is required for cytokine production and cell death in response to viral infections.
the DEAH-box RNA helicase DHX 15 contributes to the activation of MAP kinases and NF-kappaB, and to cytokine production and cell death downstream of MAVS, but not IRF-3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of RNA helicase DHX 15 in antiviral response.
the molecular basis of antiviral responses in cells and animals.
the identification of a novel RNA helicase that mediates the activation of the p38 and JNK signaling pathways downstream of MAV5 in response to poly (I:C).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DHX15 is an activator of NF-κB- and MAPK signaling pathways downstream of MAVs, but not interferons.
the DHX15 helicase is a new MAVS-dependent activator of NF-κB- and MAPK signaling pathways.

the DEAH-box RNA helicase DHX 15, which is a member of the DEAD-box RNA helicose family, plays a critical role in the activation of MAP kinase (MAPK)/nuclear factor kappa-B (NF-κ B) pathways in the innate immune system, but not in the interferon (IFN) signaling pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DHX15 is a new RNA helicase that mediates the MAVS-dependent signaling pathways downstream of RIG-I and MDA5.
DHX15 is an activator of MAPK signaling and NF-κΒ signaling in cells infected with viruses.

DHX15, a DEAH-box RNA helicase that is a member of the DExD/box helicase family, is an adaptor protein that mediates MAVS-dependent activation and apoptosis downstream of the RIG-I–MDA5 signaling pathways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DHX15 is required for MAVS-dependent activation and apoptosis in response to RNA viruses.

RNA helicases are not only important in the detection of viral RNA by RIG-I and MDA5, but are also involved in the signaling events downstream of MAVS, and that the signaling events downstream from MAVS are distinct for the different RNA helicases.
RNA helicases can activate different signaling pathways downstream of MAVV, depending on which RNA helicase they are.
